newsitem.title: USA: FERC OK's PSC Colorado, SPS merger.
newsitem.headline: FERC OK's PSC Colorado, SPS merger.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday approved the merger of Public Service Co of Colorado and Southwestern Public Service Co to form New Century Energies.
The two companies have said they plan to complete the merger this spring to create a $4 billion company, pending a nod from the Securities and Exchange Commission.
They have already won approvals from state regulators.
FERC commissioners last year raised concern that the companies' plan did not protect customers from rate increases resulting from merger costs.
It also raised concern that the merger might stifle competition in bulk power markets in the Southwest.
Those issues were addressed in a settlement between the companies and its customers and energy companies, which was endorsed by a FERC administrative law judge last December.

FERC commissioners hailed the settlement, but imposed a condition on the merger approval, saying that the companies must use an alternative dispute resolution procedure to handle any conflicts that might arise in planning the interconnection of the two transmission systems.
FERC Chairwoman Elizabeth Moler said the commission would step in if the companies did not stick to the settlement agreement and include customers in the procedure for planning the interconnection.
PSC of Colorado reached a separate agreement with the Colorado Association of Municipal Utilities, which had questioned the merger's impact on wholesale power sales.
PSC of Colorado serves Colorado and Wyoming and Southwestern serves Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Kansas.
